tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

spdc-process-wavelengths: Section 1, p.6: the paper states the 651.2 nm to 779.8 nm + 3950 nm process as its own SPDC setup; Fig. 2 and Methods agree
poling-and-temperature: Section 1, p.6 and Fig. 2 caption: 16.7 micron domain length and 32.2 +/- 0.1 C stated as the device settings
pump-pulse-and-spdc-waveguide: Fig. 2 caption, p.9: pump pulse train and 2.2-cm PPLN waveguide stated as the experimental setup
signal-detector-and-filter: Fig. 2 caption p.9 (3 nm filter set) and Methods p.20 (ID100 Si-APD, 12.5 % QE, <1.4 Hz dark count) state the signal-arm hardware
upconversion-process-and-temperature: Section 1 p.7 and Fig. 2 caption p.9: 779.8 nm + 3950 nm -> 651.2 nm in a second PPLN waveguide at 62.2 +/- 0.1 C, detected by a second Si-APD
tdc-timing: Methods, p.20: timing resolutions stated for the Si-APD and the TDC as hardware specifications
coincidence-definitions: Section 3, p.15: coincident, accidental and true coincidence are defined by the paper in its own measurement
loss-and-noise-limits: Section 2 p.13-14 and Methods p.21: the paper calls the setup 'under-optimized' (0.078 % total detection efficiency), says coupling is mainly limited by the mirror, says reducing detected modes is crucial for SNR, and ties improvement to higher-QE Si-APDs. Limitations the paper states about its own work
sun2013-def-quantum-zeno-blockade: Introduction, p.1: the paper states what it means by quantum Zeno blockade (the cited sources [18,19] back the phenomenon, but the working definition is the paper's own)
sun2013-setup-lnmicrodisk-gate: p.2, Fig. 1 discussion: the paper states its gate as an LN microdisk coupled to a prism, resonant with pump and signal
sun2013-setup-sfg-only: p.2: the paper says it considers only SFG, as a specific example
sun2013-def-cqz-regime: p.2: the paper names the CQZ regime and defines it by a resonant SF field with high intrinsic Q (Q_i^f >= Q_i^s,p), with the mechanism as stated
sun2013-def-iqz-regime: p.2: the paper names the IQZ regime and defines it by a short-lived cavity SF field, with the mechanism as stated
sun2013-scope-single-cavity-mode: p.2: the authors state their modeling restriction to one cavity mode per field and give the reason (linewidth much smaller than FSR). The radius and Q values are as printed (the text layer shows 1.5 mm and 107)
sun2013-setup-multimode-hamiltonian: p.2, Eq. (1): the paper states its own multimode model and Hamiltonian, with Upsilon as the SFG coupling coefficient
sun2013-setup-same-group-velocity-no-dec: p.2-3: the same-group-velocity assumption and the Qc << Qi assumption (decay neglected) are stated by the paper as assumptions of its model
sun2013-setup-parameter-choice: p.3: the paper states the parameters it takes (Q_i = 10^9, Q_c about 10^8, set by disk-prism distance). The relation sign for Q_c is lost in the text layer but the value says so
sun2013-setup-two-photon-state-eqs: p.3, Eq. (2): the paper states its general state and the equations derived from the Schroedinger equation, and the Schmidt decomposition with ordered eigenvalues. The paper's own model formulation
sun2013-def-gate-performance-measures: p.3: the paper defines its performance measures (squared first Schmidt coefficient and fidelity with the input signal). The text layer shows a12 for a1 squared
sun2013-setup-upsilon-overlap-integral: Supplement section II, p.6: the paper states how Upsilon is computed (overlap integral, fundamental modes q=1, l=m, energy conservation and QPM conditions)
sun2013-method-mode-search-fig2: Supplement section II, p.6: the paper states its method for Fig. 2, a numerical mode search with 15 or more combinations per radius, largest Upsilon plotted
svozil-partition-definition: p.1, Eq. (1): the paper defines the answer (kinematic) partition
svozil-partition-not-access-model: p.1: the paper states that the partition is bookkeeping, not an access model or complexity statement, and states the operational question it studies
svozil-exact-resolution-definition: p.1, Eq. (2): the paper defines exact resolution and states the orthogonality consequence
svozil-partition-zero-pattern: p.1 after Eq. (2): the paper states what its partition is and is not (sets, not subspaces; a zero pattern, not an observable)
svozil-prop1-block-discrimination: p.1-2, Proposition 1 with Eq. (5): stated with its conditions, and followed by the proof argument (necessity by orthogonal spans, sufficiency by support projectors, purification for mixed probes). The argument is short, and the paper says the result is the block form of standard conditions [2,3] and not a new general theorem
svozil-gram-block-diagonal: p.2: direct consequence of Proposition 1 (Eq. 5 constrains only cross-cell entries); singleton-cell case needs diagonal G
svozil-qe-one-and-no-advantage-by-itself: p.2: follows from Proposition 1 plus the trivial zero-query case (output independent of the instance, restated p.4). The remark that speedup needs a Q versus R gap is a definitional point. Short argument, no separate proof block
svozil-deutsch-gram-block-diagonal: p.2, Eqs. (7)-(8): explicit output states are given and the orthogonal rays follow by inspection, so the block-diagonal Gram matrix is shown. The classical two-query side of the 'familiar separation' is cited [7], not proved here
svozil-theorem1-response-spectrum: p.2, Theorem 1 with Eq. (9): stated with its conditions (any unitary V, arbitrary probes and references) and proved in the text (necessity via Eqs. 10-11, sufficiency via phase kickback and Eq. 8)
svozil-theorem1-proof-necessity: p.2, proof of Theorem 1, Eqs. (10)-(11): the necessity argument is given in the paper (reduction to z0=-p1, z1=-p0, then |z_x|<=p_x forces p=1/2 and the -1 eigenspace support). Steps are condensed but complete
svozil-theorem1-sufficiency-and-relation: p.2: sufficiency (a -1 eigenvector gives phase kickback and Eq. 8) closes Theorem 1; the sentence that the theorem fixes the four instances and varies V is the paper's own scope. The contrast with Cereceda and Meyer-Pommersheim is the authors' characterization of cited work and is not what settles this
svozil-corollary1-cyclic-response: p.3, Corollary 1, Eq. (12): follows from Theorem 1 because X_d has -1 in its spectrum exactly when d is even; D=2 is the classical depth. The odd-d upper bound of two is immediate from classical simulation. The paper gives no separate proof block but the step is immediate
svozil-qutrit-addition-removes-advantage: p.3: the d=3 case of Corollary 1, stated with scope (constant factor, not asymptotic). The closing sentence about reversibility is the authors' interpretation of that case
svozil-parity-one-query-bound: p.3, Eqs. (13)-(14): the argument is given in the paper (probe form, overlap 1-2p_i, exact separation needs p_i=1/2 for all i, normalization sum p_i <= 1, hence N <= 2). The overlap computation is stated and not expanded
svozil-aggregate-parity-oracle: p.3 after Eq. (15): the paper states that its parity result is for point access and that an aggregating oracle changes the access model; the one-query claim for that oracle is immediate
svozil-census-methods: p.3: the paper states its census method (decision-tree depth D, rational one-query feasibility, Barnum-Saks-Szegedy SDP, adaptive-tree certificates) and its own caveat that trees are not a general characterization
svozil-three-bit-majority-and-f-trees: p.3: both two-query trees are given explicitly and check (Maj3 and b1 xor b2b3), and the real multilinear degree is three, so the polynomial method (degree <= 2T) excludes one query. Construction and lower bound are both in the paper; the polynomial method is a cited tool applied here
svozil-census-contribution-and-limit: p.4: the paper states what the census contributes and that the proportions are finite-model facts, not an asymptotic speedup criterion
svozil-bv-witness-dilation: p.4, Eqs. (17)-(18): the paper defines the witness-bearing oracle and its channel
svozil-bv-witness-q1-r-nk: p.4, Eqs. (19)-(20): stated with conditions (k<n, error <1/2) and proved in the text: quantum part by Eqs. (21)-(22), classical upper bound by basis queries outside S, lower bound by the affine-space averaging argument. The paper marks it an access-induced change of the task-oracle pair
svozil-bv-witness-quantum-readout: p.4, Eqs. (21)-(22): the paper gives the reduced state after kickback and the post-Hadamard result by character orthogonality, then the zero-query argument. Steps are condensed but complete
svozil-bv-witness-classical-lower-bound: p.4 after Eq. (22): the averaging argument is given with its promise a_S=0 and uniform distribution (fewer than n-k equations leave a positive-dimension affine space; extends to internal randomness). A lower bound on a restricted input set bounds the worst case
svozil-bv-witness-extremes: p.4: the k=0 and k=n cases are immediate specializations of Eqs. (19) and (22); the n-versus-one gap at k=0 uses the cited BV result, but the stated cases follow from the paper's own equations
svozil-limit-no-asymptotic-speedup: Conclusion, p.5: the paper states that finite-census percentages cannot establish an asymptotic speedup. The Ambainis clause is attribution of a cited result and is not what settles the grade
svozil-ai-assistant-and-data-availabilit: Acknowledgements and Data availability, p.5: the paper states its own use of an AI assistant and where the code and certificates are

theory_low.simulation-modes-and-agreement: A numerical simulation (mode count about 15, coupled Heisenberg equations) compared with one measured dataset, Section 2 p.13, Fig. 4(a). Not a proof; agreement is the authors' reading and the discrepancy cause is conjecture ('likely')
theory_low.sun2013-measured-upsilon-vs-radius: p.2-3 and Fig. 2: Upsilon values are calculated (analytical WGM profiles, supplement section II), best over a numerical mode search, and Fig. 2 is a fit. A calculation result that depends on chosen modes and QPM pattern, not a proved result. Nothing here is measured, despite the id
theory_low.sun2013-mechanism-gaussian-entanglement: p.3-4: a qualitative explanation ('in a nutshell') of a Gaussian-pulse simulation result (Fig. 3), supported only by a toy model. Not proved
theory_low.sun2013-toy-model-entangled-state: p.4: an intuitive toy model, 'ideal QZB' assumed, with no derivation. The state shown has lost bra-ket symbols in the text layer. Not proved
theory_low.svozil-representation-vs-access: p.2: the Gram invariance under Eq. (6) is shown by the displayed identity, but the claim that mutually simulating families have complexities equal up to constant factors is asserted with no proof, and 'exact one-query behavior can nevertheless change' is a pointer with no statement here (the example is Theorem 1). Mixed value; not settled by the passage
theory_low.svozil-sign-oracle-and-coherent-control: p.2: the Hadamard-conjugation equivalence and global-phase point are asserted without calculation, and the coherent-control point is attributed to cited work [6] (Araujo et al.). A cited result, not proved here
theory_low.svozil-three-bit-20-of-35: p.3, Table I: the count 20 of 35 is a computed classification. Table I is consistent (3 at factor 2 plus 1+4+12 at 3/2 gives 3 and 17), but only majority and F get in-paper constructions; the rational and SDP certificates are in the external supplement archive, not in the paper
theory_low.svozil-bv-witness-coherent-and-channel: p.4: a remark with no derivation. The idea (the coupling does not depend on a) is plausible from Eq. (17), but the value ties it to the distinction between standard and garbage-bearing oracle access with a cited work (Aaronson [17]), which is an interpretation and a cited point
